subject: Acme Health commercial exception: Accelerator POC discount request
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Acme Health - commercial exception request for Accelerator POC

Hi team,

Quick summary: Acme Health (Julia Sullivan, procurement) has asked for a deeper discount for an Accelerator POC we proposed. They want a 3-month POC followed by a 12-month committed renewal. The commercial asks are: 35% off list for year 1, Dedicated capacity + VPC, and a one-time onboarding credit. Their expected first-year spend if they convert is roughly $480k ARR.

Why this matters: Acme is a reference-able enterprise in healthcare (regional payer) and they have strict security requirements (SOC2 + additional logging). If we can secure a POC with Dedicated + VPC and convert, likely a multi-year relationship. Our standard commercial guardrails cap deal-level discounts at 25% without VP/CFO sign-off. The AE is requesting an exception to 35%.

Attachments: Acme_Accelerator_Pricing_v3.xlsx (pricing worksheet), SOW_Acme_v1_redline.docx (initial redlines), security_questionnaire_acme.pdf (customer asks).

Ask: Vivek / Marissa — can you review for approval? If you want, I can tighten the commercial levers (upfront payment, minimum monthly commitment, shorter POC usage cap). I flagged Connor for contract adjustments and to prepare a conditional memo.

Notes / quick risks:
- Margin impact at 35% is material for Dedicated capacity; need offset (upfront payment + 12-month commit).
- Security checklist incomplete — they need an answer on data residency and audit log retention.

Thanks,
Monica

Monica Patel

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health - commercial exception request for Accelerator POC

Marissa — looping you in for official signoff. Monica and team, thank you for the context. I agree Acme is strategic and the POC -> committed renewal motion makes sense, but 35% is outside normal tolerance without CFO sign-off.

Proposed approval path I support in principle (pending Marissa signoff):
- Approve up to 30% discount immediately for POC + conversion if customer:
  - signs 12-month commitment post-POC, and
  - pays 50% of year-1 in advance, and
  - accepts a capped monthly consumption during the POC (we limit to X tokens / session).
- For 31-40% (i.e., their 35% ask) I need Marissa to confirm and document a credit/expense schedule to protect margin.

Connor — please prepare a short internal memo (1 page) that captures the economics and proposed contractual controls (SOW payment milestones, termination clauses, measurable POC success criteria). Monica — please confirm the HubSpot deal id and the timeline to sign so we can tie this to revenue forecasts.

Quoted for context:
> Quick summary: Acme Health (Julia Sullivan, procurement) has asked for a deeper discount for an Accelerator POC we proposed....

Regards,
Vivek

Vivek Kulkarni

vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0133
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health - commercial exception request for Accelerator POC

Thanks for the tag, Vivek. I reviewed the attached pricing worksheet and the redlines. I can approve a commercial exception up to 35% on the following strict conditions (must be included in the SOW / order form):

1) Customer commits to a 12-month term starting immediately after successful POC conversion.
2) 60% of year-1 fees collected upfront (non-refundable) — this mitigates cash and margin exposure.
3) PO C cap during trial: limit to 25% of estimated monthly production usage (we'll define token cap in the SOW).
4) Security confirmation: SOC 2 Type II evidence on file and agreement on audit-log retention (30 days minimum).
5) If they do not convert to the committed term within 45 days of POC end, a 15% catch-up fee applies for months where usage exceeded the POC cap.

I will sign off on the approval memo once Connor provides a one-page commercial exception memo that documents the ARR impact, margin delta, and the payment schedule. Please add the approval_memo_vivek_marissa.pdf to the final folder after I sign.

Monica — please confirm that Acme can and will pay upfront. If they cannot meet the 60% requirement, we drop approval to 30% only.

Marissa

Date: Fri, 17 Jul 2026 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme Health - commercial exception request for Accelerator POC

All — attaching the requested one-page memo and an updated SOW with payment milestones and the POC usage caps redlined. I included a DocuSign envelope for the order form (link below) so we can finalize quickly if Acme confirms the 60% upfront.

Key points in the memo (summary):
- List price year-1: $685,000. With 35% discount -> effective year-1 $445,250. Estimated margin delta vs standard price: -22%.
- Mitigations: 60% upfront payment, 12-month committed term, defined token cap during POC, and a clause for catch-up fees if conversion is delayed.
- Legal: reduced liability cap to $1M for the POC period and an explicit termination window tied to delivery milestones.
